errors.english: These two stages occur through the power of the mind and not through any other means.
errors.why: The verse gives the second of three means (blessing, mind, mantra, as the commentary itself lays out): the second is by the power of mind, not 'both of these'.

note: A sound rendering of the maṇḍala-site and cord commentary; only the verse on the second means of taking possession is misread as 'these two'.
Faithful rendering of the Hevajra commentary on Sukhāvatī/bhaga, the 'I' of the expounder, and the end-of-supreme-joy definition of sahaja.

errors.english: craving causes the childish being to be fully purified
errors.why: In this account of craving the verb (cf. སྲེད་པའི་ཀུན་ཏུ་སྦྱོར་བ just after) means craving binds or yokes the immature to the good destiny they want, not that it purifies them.

note: The five differences between the receptacle and birth cycles and the analysis of craving are rendered accurately apart from one verb read as 'purify'.

errors.english: And the methods that cleanse the stains of the (kleshas) mental afflictions
errors.why: The Tibetan says 'by means (methods) that are stained by the afflictions', i.e. kleśa-tainted method paired with innate wisdom, not methods that cleanse the afflictions.

fix.find: the methods that cleanse the stains of the (kleshas) mental afflictions
fix.replace: the methods stained by the (kleshas) mental afflictions

errors.english: From the lips of Guru Nirguna:
errors.why: The siddha's name is transcribed Naraguna, not Nirguna.

note: The siddha verses are rendered well, but one verse inverts kleśa-stained method into a cleansing method and one name is altered.
Faithful rendering of the Vyākhyāyukti close: the Sūtrālaṃkāra verse, the five qualities of the Buddha's speech and the two speakers' two purities.
The ten perfections, the guard against nihilism and the non-abiding nirvāṇa passage are rendered faithfully.
Accurate rendering of the synonym series for the inconceivable/unborn/dharma-dhātu with dhātu correctly explained as gotra/cause.

errors.english: It is not through (mudras) symbolic hand gestures or physical postures
errors.why: In this polemic against consort practice (cf. ཕྱག་རྒྱ་སྦྱོར་བ on the previous side) ཕྱག་རྒྱ is the (karma)mudrā partner, not hand gestures.

errors.english: Since those were spoken for the sake of the students,
errors.why: The line says 'what is called the disciple's empowerment, why should this too not be refuted?', so the disciple's empowerment is the subject being refuted, not a reason.

errors.english: The fourth [note: section or chapter] was composed by the Master (Drolma) Tara,
errors.why: The scholar of the East (agentive ཡིས) is the subject of a sentence continuing on the next side (does not know even the mere talk of the fourth [empowerment] taught by Tārā); it is not a colophon making Tārā the scholar, and 'the fourth' is the fourth empowerment, not a chapter.

note: A difficult polemical verse text whose opening is broadly followed, but the argument against consort practice and the closing lines are partly misparsed.

errors.why: དབང་པོའི་ཏོག is Indra's banner (indradhvaja), the festival standard watched by spectators, not a 'crest of the senses'.

errors.english: it was out of joy, yet not without respect
errors.why: The Tibetan says 'it was affection, and not respect', mirroring the previous line; the English negates it into 'not without respect'.

note: The Licchavis' lament is rendered vividly, but Indra's banner is lost and the respect/affection antithesis is reversed.

errors.english: If one perceives them as profound without conceptualizing them
errors.why: Both the notion of profundity and conceptualization are negated (as in the parallel ཟབ་པའི་འདུ་ཤེས་མེད་ཅིང་ and གཏིང་དཔག་དཀའ་བའི་འདུ་ཤེས་ཀྱང་མེད་ཅིང་): one engages in the perfection only if one has no perception of them as profound.

fix.find: If one perceives them as profound without conceptualizing them
fix.replace: If one has neither the perception that they are profound nor any conceptualization of them

note: A faithful rendering of the commentary on 'profound' and 'unfathomable', except that the first gloss says one perceives phenomena as profound when the text says one does not.
